15 The derivation of the pressure equation p =  gh uses a number of relationships between
quantities.
Which relationship is not used in the derivation of this equation?
mass
A
density = volume
B
potential energy = mass  acceleration of free fall  height
force
C
pressure = area
D
weight = mass  acceleration of free fall

hints: Notice that $\Delta p = \rho g \Delta h$ contains density $\rho$, $g$ and height $\Delta h$, but no energy term.
Picture the derivation as a vertical column of fluid with cross-sectional area $A$ and height $\Delta h$, so volume is $A\Delta h$.
Track how mass becomes weight and then pressure using $m$, $W = mg$ and $p = F/A$, and check which listed relationship about potential energy is left over.
walkthrough: Consider a vertical column of fluid of cross-sectional area $A$ and height $\Delta h$, so its volume is $V = A\Delta h$.
Use density $\rho = m/V$ rearranged to $m = \rho V = \rho A \Delta h$ to get the mass of this column.
Use weight $W = mg$ to get the force due to the column as $W = \rho A \Delta h g$.
Use pressure $p = F/A$ with $F = W$, so $\Delta p = W/A = \rho A \Delta h g / A = \rho g \Delta h$.
No step uses potential energy $= \text{mass} \times g \times \text{height}$, so that relationship is not used. This is option B.

A.explanation: This is used to write the mass of the fluid column as $m = \rho V = \rho A \Delta h$.

B.explanation: Gravitational potential energy $mgh$ is not needed because the derivation uses the weight force directly, not energy.

C.explanation: This is used as $\Delta p = F/A$, where the force is the weight of fluid above.

D.explanation: This is used to write the weight of the fluid column as $W = mg$.
